scope: Primary-source prerequisite review of exactly the sixteen staged Hugging Face original documents, in index order. All 4042 numbered original lines were read completely in small chunks; aggregate source delimiters are not original lines. The staged text contains address placeholders; original identifiers and SHA-256 values below are preserved from the supplied index, not recomputed from the transformed text. Default frozen runtime: isolated, non-root, offline, standard-library Python. Reviewed-offline expansion is approved in principle, not installed or demonstrated here. Before task freeze, review the actual unchanged public inputs, dependencies and their licenses, command controls, and independent verifiers. No source example, helper, import, training, benchmark, inference, installation, cloud operation, credential access, network service, or additional agent was executed or invoked. Reading and report-validation operations are not workflow execution credit. No permanent source exclusion is credited.
linked_reference_caveat: Only these sixteen original documents were read. Every linked reference, helper, production template, requirements file, catalog, model card, model artifact, dataset, package implementation, and service contract outside them remains unread and unverified. Descriptions such as production-ready, auto-detected, latest, supported, verified, pricing, plan eligibility, and hardware availability are source claims, not independently established facts. This review neither follows linked instructions nor grants execution approval. An offline reimplementation, manifest check, card draft, or stub is not evidence of training, published model evaluation, working cloud deployment, or real inference. Actual unchanged public artifacts and dependency closures, licenses, command side effects and independent acceptance tests must be reviewed before freezing any expanded offline task; absent evidence is a review dependency, not a permanent exclusion.

sources.workflow: Generated reference for the hf command family: local environment/version/cache operations alongside Hub discovery, authenticated uploads and repository changes, jobs, experimental cloud sandboxes, endpoints, storage, and extensions. The document says it was generated with huggingface_hub v2.0.0; the imperative installation and update snippets are inert research data.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Actual CLI execution requires the relevant installed hf implementation; standard-library Python alone does not provide it. Cache operations need a real local cache or directory. Hub retrieval and on-demand mounts need network access and existing repositories or buckets. Authentication is available through HF_TOKEN or stored login, with authorization depending on the operation and resource; not every local or public-read command requires a token. Cloud execution needs the selected hardware/image/script and service access; deployments add model, framework, region, instance and engine configuration. Mounting uses a separate hf-mount utility. Extension installation can introduce executable third-party code.
sources.offline_assessment: Feasible candidates include command-plan analysis, local cache manifest/checksum reasoning and argument validation against reviewed unchanged public records. Real hf local-cache behavior could be tested only after reviewing and freezing the CLI dependency closure and cache artifacts. A GPU, weights, or hosted account is not needed for a purely local command/configuration task. No local parser or dry-run transcript proves that remote jobs, synchronization, uploads, mounts, or deployments work. Deny auth-token printing, installation/update/extension execution, deletion/pruning, remote writes and cloud process controls by default; even dry-run implementation behavior needs review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use an independent expected argument/side-effect oracle and before/after hashes of disposable public cache fixtures; verify checksums against trusted manifests rather than trusting a self-reported success. Resolve actual CLI-version flag support and differences from the Spaces document before freeze. For any future genuinely remote objective, separately require authorized service-side resource and artifact evidence plus functional output checks; that is outside this review and earns no credit now.

sources.workflow: Discover AWS profile and region, validate credentials through STS, obtain account and caller identity, classify IAM-user versus assumed-role/SSO principals, and report missing or expired context before later deployment work. It prefers effective CLI configuration over guessing or hardcoded region defaults.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Profile precedence is user-specified profile over AWS_PROFILE over default. Region precedence is explicit user region, AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, then active-profile configuration; no value requires clarification. Real identity validation requires the AWS CLI, usable credentials and STS connectivity. Reading an ARN can identify a principal class but does not establish its actual permissions: the statement that SSO principals typically cannot write IAM is a source generalization. Deployment roles are discussed as a later concern, not something this discovery task creates.
sources.offline_assessment: A useful source-faithful local subtask can resolve precedence and classify supplied configuration/identity records using standard-library parsing, without weights, GPU, a hosted account, or real credentials. Use only reviewed unchanged public examples, not the user's actual configuration or environment. Recorded identity JSON can be analyzed but cannot validate current credentials or prove access to an account. Do not run aws configure or STS during this research.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently authored public fixtures should cover profile override, missing profile, every region precedence branch, absent region, malformed identity, and principal classes. Verify no real environment or credential files are read and no external command/network path exists. Actual credential validity and IAM capability would require separately authorized service evidence, not an ARN heuristic or a mocked response.

sources.workflow: Prepare an isolated Python environment for SageMaker automation, install orchestration dependencies, invoke that environment's interpreter explicitly, and inspect package metadata versions. It distinguishes direct-boto3 bundled scripts from optional SageMaker SDK usage and describes platform-specific interpreter paths.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source selects Python 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12, defaults setup to 3.12, and asks for current boto3/awscli rather than package pins. Its unread setup helper reportedly detects uv, otherwise uses venv, installs an unread requirements file and may recreate mismatched environments. Version checking uses importlib.metadata. huggingface_hub and transformers are conditional extras; the SageMaker SDK is optional, not required by the bundled deploy helpers. Real package setup requires package artifacts and writable isolated storage, but not itself weights, a GPU or a cloud account.
sources.offline_assessment: Standard-library work can inspect supplied package metadata, validate interpreter/configuration plans and reason about environment isolation. Actual offline setup is a possible reviewed expansion only with an unchanged, licensed, compatible local package closure and controlled installation locations; the source's floating latest instructions are not a reproducible freeze specification. No package is installed and no unread setup/version helper is run here. Successful metadata parsing alone is not a working deployment environment.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Review the actual setup/check helpers and requirements before executing them, especially deletion/recreation, subprocesses, installation sources and interpreter selection. Independently check selected interpreter, isolation from system site-packages, exact artifact hashes, package metadata and expected API compatibility without AWS calls. SDK routing and SSO-regression statements remain source claims until separately checked against reviewed evidence.

sources.workflow: Select a SageMaker serving-image family and regional image identifier from the official DLC catalog, prefer compatible Hugging Face images with documented exceptions, distinguish encoder from generative rerankers, and configure image/instance/CUDA/AMI and serving environment contracts. The document also describes catalog fallbacks and image mirroring.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Selection needs actual model architecture/task metadata, compatible catalog rows, target region and instance, and account/region image availability. The source requires a particular AMI for cu130-or-later vLLM images, host binding and model selection variables; gated models require an appropriate token unless artifacts are pre-staged. Real serving additionally needs the container, compatible runtime/hardware, model artifacts and authorized SageMaker resources; CPU TEI and CPU toolkit paths exist, so a GPU is not universal. Mirroring uses Docker, AWS CLI and registry permissions. Custom model code must be reviewed and pinned before enabling trust-remote-code.
sources.offline_assessment: Model-to-image and AMI/environment validation can be an offline standard-library task over unchanged public configuration and frozen catalog records; no weights or real account are necessary for that bounded decision task. An approved expansion could inspect reviewed container metadata, but cannot infer functional serving merely from its manifest. Do not fetch catalogs, run mirror/deploy helpers or pull images here. The archived-TGI, catalog-availability, broken-GPU-image and CUDA-compatibility statements are dated source claims; the cu129/g5 AMI workaround is explicitly unverified in the source.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent compatibility oracle should check task and architecture together, CPU/GPU variant, regional account identifiers, allowed fallback reasons, AMI selection and safe model-code defaults. Review all actual catalog/model inputs and unread deploy/mirror helpers before freeze. For real serving, independent request/output tests and worker logs are required: the source warns that a ping/InService state can coexist with a broken Python worker. Neither a selected image nor a mock health response proves deployment or inference.

sources.workflow: Use a connected Hugging Face MCP server for model/dataset/Space/paper discovery, repository details and documentation, then optionally invoke hosted Gradio tools, generate images, submit compute jobs or schedule jobs. It is an example and tool-selection guide, not an implementation of those services.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Actual use requires an MCP client/server connection with the described tools and network access. Public discovery does not intrinsically require local model weights or a GPU. Hosted Space inference requires a functioning remote app and its parameter schema; compute requires supported hardware, image or script dependencies and service entitlement. The examples pass HF_TOKEN as a job secret for private repositories. Authorization, payment and execution requirements depend on the selected remote operation; the document does not establish them all.
sources.offline_assessment: A bounded tool-routing or recorded-result analysis task can be performed offline with reviewed unchanged public schemas and results. Standard-library code can validate argument shapes and identify operations that would mutate resources. Stubs may test routing but cannot establish a working MCP connection, successful remote training, image generation, current search results or usable hosted inference. All jobs, scheduling and dynamic invocation examples remain unexecuted.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Review real tool schemas/server implementations, response provenance and argument handling before freezing a routing task. Independently compare tool choices and composed arguments to expected public cases, ensure secrets are absent and enforce a no-network/no-submission boundary. Actual hosted results would need independently attributable service artifacts and semantic checks, not a fabricated job identifier or canned response; the server setup and linked documentation remain unread.

sources.workflow: Parse task/device constraints, discover relevant official benchmark datasets, collect existing leaderboard scores, enrich candidates with parameter counts and license tags, filter/rank and produce a comparison table. This workflow consumes published records; it does not run the benchmarks or models it recommends.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The live examples use curl, jq, a stored token and Hub metadata/leaderboard services, with hf as an alternate model-info path. Ranking needs relevant leaderboard records and model metadata; device filtering is conditional on a supplied memory constraint. Missing safetensors data falls back to a model-name size guess. The source supplies approximate fp16/Q4 weight-memory budgets and an API-only distinction. Neither local weights, a GPU nor inference credentials are required merely to analyze existing public benchmark results; source example authentication should not be generalized into a universal public-read requirement.
sources.offline_assessment: Strong offline candidate: rank and join unchanged public leaderboard and model metadata snapshots with standard-library JSON processing, preserve unavailable scores and provenance, and distinguish popularity fallback from benchmark evidence. Review actual snapshot licenses and completeness before freeze. Memory estimates are heuristics, not demonstrated device fit or inference speed; include runtime overhead uncertainty. The text mentions a curated fallback table that is not present in this original, so do not invent its content or silently substitute recommendations.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check cross-benchmark model joins, metric direction/scale, missing data, verified flags, ties, device/no-device branches, parameter parsing and API-only filtering. Validate licenses against actual reviewed license materials rather than a tag alone, and preserve snapshot date and score provenance. No recomputed table validates published benchmark methodology or proves the recommended model runs on the stated device; those need separate evidence and tasks.

sources.workflow: Run inspect-ai or lighteval evaluations using a local inference backend, choose vLLM versus Transformers/accelerate, start with limited samples and scale after a smoke test. A provider-backed path runs the evaluation driver locally but depends on remote inference. Publishing, model-card edits and Jobs orchestration are explicitly outside this skill's scope.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Real local-model evaluation needs compatible framework/backend dependencies, actual model/tokenizer artifacts, task datasets and enough memory/compute for the chosen model. The source recommends uv and GPU-access checks for GPU runs, supplies Apple Silicon/small-model guidance and does not establish that every evaluation requires NVIDIA hardware. HF_TOKEN is specified for gated/private models. Provider-backed evaluation needs model coverage, service access and applicable authorization instead of direct local GPU control. Referenced scripts and inspect-evals task implementations are not included in the staged original.
sources.offline_assessment: Configuration selection and analysis of existing reviewed public evaluation logs can run in the default runtime without weights or a hosted account. A real offline evaluation would require a separately reviewed dependency/model/dataset closure and feasible hardware; no such closure is supplied or approved by this review. A source limited-sample smoke test is not a full benchmark, and parsing logs is not a new evaluation. The source's trust-remote-code examples do not authorize execution; any custom model or task code requires prior review and isolation.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Review all three actual runner scripts, task loaders, scorer implementations, model code and side effects before freeze. Independently verify exact model revision, task version, dataset split, sample limits, prompt/chat-template settings, backend, generated responses and scoring against expected cases. Preserve which results are recorded versus newly produced, and distinguish provider inference from local inference. Published evaluation or publication success cannot be inferred from a stubbed runner or a log-shaped file.

sources.workflow: Build Python web UIs with Interface, Blocks and ChatInterface; define components, custom HTML and event listeners; optionally discover and call existing Gradio application endpoints using the CLI. The greeting, echo and rating examples are ordinary application logic rather than model inference.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: A functioning Gradio app needs Python plus a compatible gradio installation and local serving/client capability. Custom HTML interaction needs a suitable browser and any referenced assets; the rating example includes an external image asset. Model dependencies, weights, GPUs and hosted accounts are conditional on the callback, not requirements for all Gradio interfaces. CLI calls to hosted apps require reachable service/schema and token authorization only for private Spaces; file inputs can upload user data. Detailed guides and examples are linked but unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Default-runtime candidates include reviewing event wiring, validating a public component specification or testing extracted deterministic callback logic, with no ML hardware or account. Actually running an offline UI requires a reviewed Gradio dependency closure, local-only launch controls and any browser/assets, an approved expansion not performed here. Do not launch servers, follow CLI prediction examples or fetch assets during this research. Static source validity or an echo callback alone is not a verified working browser UI or real model inference.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: For a bounded code task, independently test callback edge cases and event input/output mapping against an explicit specification. For real UI credit, require reviewed framework-version compatibility, isolated local interaction tests, event dispatch/output checks and absence of external requests/uploads or public sharing. Inspect custom HTML/JS and asset provenance/licenses; hosted endpoint discovery or a successful HTTP response alone does not verify output semantics.

sources.workflow: Extract a paper identifier, retrieve paper markdown or structured metadata, find linked repositories and summarize/analyze the actual paper. The document additionally describes authenticated authorship claims, indexing and link updates, which are distinct write operations rather than necessary parts of reading a paper.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Live public paper reading needs connectivity, an indexed paper and an HTTP client; public paper pages explicitly require no authentication. Full markdown relies on the paper's HTML availability and can instead return only the Hub paper page; missing detail requires another actual source. Writes require HF_TOKEN and applicable authorship/submitter/admin authority; identifiers and version suffixes need care. There is no model-weight, GPU, training framework or paid-cloud prerequisite for parsing identifiers or analyzing already supplied public paper text.
sources.offline_assessment: Identifier parsing, metadata joins and provenance-aware analysis of unchanged public paper text/JSON are plausible standard-library offline tasks after input/license review. The present sixteen originals do not supply the actual research papers or API response corpus. Do not mistake an abstract, AI-generated summary or landing-page fallback for complete paper content. No live retrieval, indexing, authorship claim or link mutation was attempted, and an offline metadata/card draft does not publish or index anything.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use independent expected identifier cases, including versions and invalid inputs, and compare extracted metadata to reviewed source snapshots. A content-provenance verifier must distinguish full paper, landing page, abstract and generated summary, then check analytical claims against the actual supplied paper. Any eventual write task needs separately authorized ownership and service-side change verification; parsing a successful-looking response is insufficient and outside current credit.

It also recommends source inspection and refers to specialized references for ZeroGPU, dependencies, debugging and grants.

Gradio/Docker and selected inference paths need corresponding runtime/dependencies and model artifacts, with conditional tokens for gated models/providers. sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check SDK/frontmatter constraints, actual versioned CLI schemas, dependency compatibility, file routing, visibility/secrets separation and local output behavior. Resolve source-reported policies and platform versions from reviewed frozen evidence before task freeze; referenced debug/requirements/model helpers remain unread. It requires help text, non-destructive testing and examples, prefers shell but allows Python/TSX, and lists unread baseline and enrichment helpers.

sources.workflow: Fine-tune object detectors, image classifiers and prompted SAM/SAM2 segmentation models, primarily on paid HF Jobs GPUs, with dataset inspection, training-argument configuration, time/cost/hardware selection, monitoring and Hub persistence. It also mentions local training. The original delegates actual training/preprocessing/evaluation behavior to unread scripts and references.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Its cloud checklist requires eligible paid plan, authenticated write token, secret propagation, existing Hub dataset and enabled artifact push. Detection needs objects.bbox/category, classification image/label, and segmentation images/masks plus bbox/point prompts; exact formats and split handling matter. Actual fine-tuning needs pretrained model/processor artifacts, data, PEP 723 dependency closure and fitting compute. The source recommends T4 for many small models and larger GPUs for some SAM choices; no local GPU is required when cloud compute is used. It distinguishes MCP versus Python submission semantics, explicit hub_token injection, required parser flags and long enough timeouts. Trackio introduces monitoring side effects.
sources.offline_assessment: Dataset schema/bbox/prompt validation, configuration checks and recorded-metric analysis may be feasible offline without weights, GPU or account, using unchanged reviewed public annotations and independent expectations. Image decoding or actual training would require reviewed dependency/model/data artifacts beyond the default runtime. Do not run the inspector, cost helper, training templates, trackers, submit jobs or push outputs here. Claims that scripts automatically sanitize boxes, remap labels, handle single-class metrics or save models remain unverified. A valid annotation manifest or canned metrics is not trained weights or real evaluation.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Review actual inspector, three training scripts, loss/metric implementations, persistence helpers, dependencies and dataset/model licenses before freeze. Independently check bbox interpretation/conversion, category mapping, image-mask/prompt alignment, split leakage, parser booleans, timeouts and secret-free offline controls. For genuine training credit require attributable changed checkpoints, nonzero optimizer work, independently computed held-out mAP/accuracy/segmentation metrics and reloadable artifacts; Hub persistence would need separate authorized artifact evidence. The source's claimed model quality, cost and timing are not acceptance evidence.

sources.workflow: Write/review Gradio ZeroGPU handlers with controlled GPU allocation, duration/quota sizing, eager model registration, process-boundary-safe state and outputs, concurrency safety, compatible CUDA wheels and Python/dependency configuration. The source says the decorator is a no-op off-platform, which does not reproduce the hosted scheduler.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Actual ZeroGPU behavior needs a Gradio SDK Space on ZeroGPU hardware, platform eligibility/quota, the spaces runtime and suitable model/data/dependency artifacts for its workload. Real GPU computation occurs inside decorated calls; the source warns that a patched CUDA-availability check is not hardware evidence. CPU/local code can use the decorator as a passthrough with the package present, without a hosted account. Picklable boundaries, CPU-returned tensors, concurrency-safe state, duration/size constraints and wheel/torch ABI matching matter. It specifies Python pinning and platform-managed spaces dependencies, while current hardware and supported versions are deferred to unread references.
sources.offline_assessment: Standard-library candidates include source/configuration review, duration arithmetic and state/concurrency reasoning over public examples. Reviewed local dependencies could allow genuine off-platform handler tests but cannot establish ZeroGPU allocation, worker reuse, quota or GPU inference. Note internal/source tensions before freeze: eager CUDA placement versus portable device-selection advice, and the description's no-runtime-nvcc framing versus the body explicitly saying runtime nvcc exists while build-time nvcc does not. Do not install wheels, invoke CUDA, launch apps or test a live Space. Parsing metadata or mocking spaces.GPU earns no hosted execution credit.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Read the actual concurrency, lifecycle, quota and CUDA/dependency references and runtime implementation before making executable acceptance claims. Independently test deterministic duration boundaries and lightweight state logic; never unpickle untrusted public artifacts. A genuine expanded local handler test needs race/state-isolation checks and licensed reviewed packages. Hosted acceptance would additionally need independent allocation/process/CPU-return/output evidence and current policy checks, not patched is_available, a no-op decorator or a fake quota response.

sources.workflow: Route dense bi-encoder, cross-encoder, sparse SPLADE or late-interaction multi-vector training to per-type references/templates; choose matching data/loss/evaluator, record baseline, smoke-test, train and emit a scored verdict with logs and Hub publishing. The original explicitly says it is a router and must not be used alone to synthesize a complete training script.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source specifies sentence-transformers train extras at least version 5, at least version 6 for MultiVectorEncoder, conditional multimodal extras and an optional tracker. Real training needs a matching base model, data, losses/evaluators and feasible memory/compute. GPU is strongly recommended; CPU demos and SentenceTransformer StaticEmbedding are explicitly possible. Default execution is local, with HF Jobs only if needed. Write-scoped authentication is for Hub push, not an intrinsic requirement of local computation. Mandatory unread references cover data shapes, metrics, precision and templates; hardware/Jobs/prompt-prefix references are conditional.
sources.offline_assessment: Configuration/loss-data-shape checks and analysis of existing baseline/verdict records may be offline candidates without weights, GPU or hosted account, after actual public inputs are reviewed. Real offline small-model or StaticEmbedding training is not permanently excluded but requires inspected per-type references/templates, dependencies, licensed model/data artifacts, capacity and a real verifier. Do not invent missing scaffolding or treat a one-step planned smoke test as completed training. The default end-of-run push and telemetry/logging behavior must be disabled or redirected under reviewed controls for any future offline task.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Review all required per-type and cross-cutting files before freeze; names and summaries in this router do not establish implementation correctness. Independently verify baseline timing, held-out split, evaluator metric keys/direction, loss-data compatibility, checkpoint changes and output reloadability. Sparse tasks additionally need sparsity dimensions; multi-vector tasks need correct scoring/scale and MaxSim evaluation. A printed WIN line is not independent proof of learning or generalization, and a model-card draft is not Hub publication.
